positioning_001: Blockbuster had the same movies as Netflix in 2007. Netflix won because it owned a positioning — unlimited, no late fees, delivered to your door — that Blockbuster could not copy without destroying its existing business model.
capital_001: During the 2008 financial crisis, companies with 18+ months of runway made acquisitions and hired talent at historic discounts. Companies with 3 months of runway made desperate decisions. The difference was capital position, not revenue.
capital_002: Amazon ran at near-zero margins for a decade not because it was unprofitable but because it was deliberately deploying every dollar into infrastructure. The Capital lever was being spent on the future, not the present.
people_001: When Steve Jobs returned to Apple in 1997, he cut 70% of Apple's product line. He did not trust the system — he trusted a few specific people. That was the right call at that stage. At scale it became the ceiling. Apple's greatest products after 2011 came from teams Jobs had built, not from Jobs himself.
intel_001: Netflix analyzed viewing data in 2011 and discovered that subscribers who watched political dramas also watched films directed by David Fincher and starring Kevin Spacey. No other studio had that insight. House of Cards was not a creative bet — it was an Information Asymmetry play.
comms_001: When United Airlines broke a musician's guitar and refused to compensate him, he posted a song about it on YouTube. It reached 150,000 views in one day. United's stock dropped 10% within four days. Their Communications lever was at zero when it mattered most.
differentiation_001: When Starbucks entered the UK market, local coffee chains panicked about price competition. Starbucks was more expensive. They won anyway because the experience — the language, the cups, the ambiance — was different enough that price became irrelevant for their specific customer.
habit_001: Duolingo's retention is not about language learning. It is about streaks. The streak mechanic is a trigger-investment loop — miss a day and you lose something you built. That is not language psychology. That is Habit Design.
systems_001: McDonald's does not hire exceptional cooks. It builds exceptional systems that allow ordinary people to deliver a consistent product at scale. The system is the product. Ray Kroc's insight was not the hamburger — it was the process.
intel_002: When Apple launched the iPhone in 2007, every major carrier and handset manufacturer dismissed it as too expensive and too limited. Nokia had 40% of the global handset market. They were measuring the market they knew. Apple was measuring the market that was coming.
